recommendations.rationale: Defer selecting any numerical check to the check phase. A prediction_braking probe at one saved projected state near the terminal window (update 34 has effective_horizon 1, matching a 0.01 s authorized horizon) under the granted configuration (model.gvs@1.0.0, implicit_euler, integration_step_s 0.002, horizon_s 0.01, saved_state_or_temporary_analysis) could compare the recorded applied tension with an instantaneous braking-box input and measure a local endpoint speed difference; per its documented limits it cannot by itself separate objective weighting, seed selection, horizon effects or backend-model mismatch, and a 10 ms projected-model probe cannot explain the whole settling failure.

Defer any control-parameter change. Although terminal_tip_speed_weight is recorded as 0.0 and the velocity weights as 1e-4, raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance without actual contributions/scaling, and the full warm plans and optimizer traces needed to see plan-level braking are not retained; a local_comparison at one saved state/horizon with exactly one adopted weight change could measure a local plan and endpoint difference but would not establish closed-loop settling or causality.

Defer to a later phase the question of aligning the reach and settling success criteria and of retaining control_snapshots.json (full warm plans/optimizer traces) so that any future check has matched-horizon saved states and plan-level evidence; this is a data-availability prerequisite, not authorization to change production configuration.

attribution.reason: The reach check uses a position tolerance equal to the settling position limit (0.01 m) and is reported passed, whereas the settling criterion additionally requires speed <=0.02 m/s sustained over a 0.05 s window; a residual terminal speed of 0.635 m/s therefore fails a condition the reach check does not test, so terminal reach and settling are not equivalent objectives.

terminal_tip_speed_weight and holding_tip_speed_weight are recorded as 0.0 and the velocity weights as 1e-4 against a tracking weight of 1.0, which is consistent with a position-oriented reach objective that does not strongly reward braking; however raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance without actual contributions/scaling, and the full warm plans are not retained, so this is not certified.

Most solves terminate on User_Requested_Stop with policy_stop_reason budget_best_feasible or relative_seed_improvement and later accepted updates carry reduced effective horizons (down to 1 interval), consistent with accepted plans that do not extend a braking segment; horizon reduction could equally follow from seed selection or termination policy, so this does not identify the dominant cause.

The host scheduling statement supplied with this request specifies that synchronous controller calls complete before fixed-count backend steps and that wall deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time, so the recorded mean_update_s≈17 s against the 0.01 s control period cannot itself explain the simulated speed residual at the terminal sample.

Recorded per-interval comparisons of projected-GVS predicted versus reconstructed backend tip velocity differ (vector-difference norms of ≈0.019, ≈0.038 and ≈0.124 m/s on sampled intervals) and projected-state curvature differences are recorded at ≈0.13-0.43 rad/m, so a projected-model versus full-backend discrepancy is plausible; these aligned-interval statistics are matched-timestamp endpoint comparisons, not full state agreement, and no bounded check in this phase can separate model mismatch from weighting or horizon effects when they predict the same endpoint.

facts.statement: Retained summary reports reach_passed=true with terminal_error_m≈0.00764 m inside the reach tolerance 0.01 m, while terminal_speed_m_s≈0.635 m/s and late_max_speed_m_s≈1.581 m/s both exceed the settling speed limit 0.02 m/s; the settling criterion pairs a 0.01 m position limit with that 0.02 m/s speed limit over a 0.05 s window, and the final-window motion samples show speed falling from ≈1.58 m/s at t=0.33 s to ≈0.635 m/s at t=0.35 s.

The saved controller recipe records terminal_tip_speed_weight=0.0, holding_tip_speed_weight=0.0, terminal_velocity_weight=1e-4, velocity_weight=1e-4, and tip_speed_scale_m_s=0.02 m/s (equal to the settling speed limit 0.02 m/s).

Of the retained solver statuses, 34 of 35 are User_Requested_Stop and 1 is Solve_Succeeded; sampled later updates report selection.policy_stop_reason budget_best_feasible or relative_seed_improvement, with the recipe's feasible-return budget_s 15.0 and relative_improvement 0.1.
Recorded effective_horizon values on later sampled updates are 5, 4, 3 and 1 control intervals versus the configured recipe horizon of 10, and mean_update_s≈17.08 s is recorded for the run.

limitations: Wall-clock deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time (host scheduling statement), so run-time facts are reported as recorded timing, not as a physical-delay mechanism.
Full historical warm plans and optimizer iteration traces are not retained (control_snapshots.json), so cost-term contributions and any planned braking segment cannot be inspected.
Recorded raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance without actual cost contributions or scaling.

Sampled settling window and terminal reach are single-execution observations; a single execution and model comparisons do not establish a dominant cause, and no causal certification or closed-loop counterfactual replay is available.
Aligned-interval predicted-versus-measured quantities compare a projected GVS prediction with a full serial-backend endpoint at matching timestamps, not full state agreement.
